[Currently]{.eyebrow}

I am a **Lecturer in Social Statistics at the University of Manchester**, where my research focuses on Bayesian statistical methodology, survey inference, data integration and computational statistics.

My current work explores how probability and non-probability data sources can be combined to improve statistical inference, how information theory can guide data collection and integration, and how artificial intelligence can support rigorous and reproducible social science research.

Alongside my research, I teach postgraduate courses in statistics, machine learning and advanced quantitative methods, develop open-source computational resources, and write about data science and artificial intelligence.

## Research Interests {.section-title}

:::: {.pillars}

::: {.pillar}
### Bayesian Statistics

Bayesian modelling, hierarchical models, posterior inference and uncertainty quantification.
:::

::: {.pillar}
### Survey Data Integration

Integration of probability and non-probability samples, selection bias and population-level inference.
:::

::: {.pillar}
### Information Theory and Adaptive Survey Design

Entropy-based stopping rules, estimand-aware prioritisation and information-driven data collection.
:::

::: {.pillar}
### Artificial Intelligence and Computational Social Science

AI-augmented data, statistical validity, machine learning and reproducible computational methodology.
:::
